info.name: DSS — POST /v1/turns:stream
info.description:
Streaming turn endpoint. One request envelope in, N claim events out, then exactly one terminal event.

Contract: docs/api-contracts/api-contract.md §4 (request), §5 (response).

Set the collection variables `base_url`, `session_id` and `trace_id` before running.

Note on Postman and SSE: Postman renders `text/event-stream` as one accumulated body rather than as discrete events. Use `curl -N` to see frames arrive in real time.

variable.description: DSS base URL. Internal only — the Experience API is the sole permitted caller (§2.3).
Per-turn correlation id. Optional — the DSS mints one when absent.

request.description:
The normal path. One ask, one Provider, one claim.

Expected frames:

```
event: claim
data: {"text":"इस सप्ताह आनंद मंडी में गेहूं का भाव ₹2,275 प्रति क्विंटल है।","source_id":"1"}

event: turn.completed
data: {"status":"answered","cause":null,"text":"…","sources":[{"id":"1","name":"Agmarknet","kind":"provider","url":"https://agmarknet.gov.in/..."}],"confidence":"high","limitations":[],"refused":[],"missing":[],"trace_id":"trc_9f2b7c1a"}
```

Only an answered turn streams. A rejected turn sends the terminal event alone.

`X-Trace-Id` is omitted, so the DSS mints one and returns it in the body.

Still HTTP 200 — the outcome lives in `status`, not the status code (§2.6).

Expected frames:

```
event: turn.rejected
data: {"status":"rejected","cause":"unsafe_illegal","text":"I can only answer agriculture and livestock related questions.","sources":[],"confidence":"high","limitations":[],"refused":[{"what":"making explosives","reason":"unsafe"}],"missing":[],"trace_id":"trc_minted_4a1f"}
```

No commodity named, so no step can be built. Nothing was answered, and `missing` has entries — that is `needs_clarification`, not `no_match` (§5.2 status table).

Expected frames:

```
event: turn.clarification
data: {"status":"needs_clarification","cause":"ambiguous","text":"Which crop's price would you like?","sources":[],"confidence":"low","limitations":[],"refused":[],"missing":[{"name":"commodity.code"}],"trace_id":"trc_minted_7b2e"}
```

item.name: 5. No match — nothing can serve it

request.description:
An ACT ask. Every network schema type today is advisory, observation, or resource — nothing books or submits. So Provider Discovery finds nothing and no step is emitted.

Nothing answered, nothing missing → `no_match`.

Expected frames:

```
event: turn.no_match
data: {"status":"no_match","cause":"unsupported_action_type","text":"I cannot book visits yet. I can answer questions about livestock care.","sources":[],"confidence":"low","limitations":[],"refused":[],"missing":[],"trace_id":"trc_minted_c390"}
```

A Provider was reachable at discovery and failed at execution.

Still HTTP 200 — the DSS processed the turn. A terminal event always arrives before the stream closes, which is how a caller tells a failure from a dropped connection (§5.3).

Expected frames:

```
event: turn.error
data: {"status":"error","cause":"provider_unavailable","text":"I am unable to process your request right now. Please try again later.","sources":[],"confidence":"low","limitations":[],"refused":[],"missing":[],"trace_id":"trc_minted_e551"}
```

item.name: 7. Follow-up turn — history carried by the caller

request.description:
"it" resolves against history. The DSS never stores history — the caller sends it every turn (§4), and the DSS treats it as untrusted data, never instructions.

Same `X-Session-Id` as turn 2, so the two turns join in the audit trail.

Expected frames:

```
event: claim
data: {"text":"Sow potato in Gujarat from mid-October to mid-November.","source_id":"1"}

event: turn.completed
data: {"status":"answered","cause":null,"text":"…","sources":[{"id":"1","name":"ICAR Potato Guide","kind":"document","url":"…"}],"confidence":"high","limitations":[],"refused":[],"missing":[],"trace_id":"trc_minted_f012"}
```

`X-Session-Id` is required (§2.1). A missing required header is a transport fault, so this is one of the few non-200 cases.

Expected: `400`, no SSE stream, a plain JSON error body.

Other non-2xx codes (§2.6):

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | unparseable body, missing required header |
| 422 | well-formed but invalid field — e.g. `channel: "fax"` |
| 429 | global concurrency cap reached; carries `Retry-After` |
| 503 | DSS unavailable or overloaded |

The DSS never returns 401 or 403 — authentication belongs to the Experience edge (§2.3).
